name: South African citizenship by naturalisation (South African Citizenship Act 88 of 1995)

requirement_groups.name: General track, 5 years on permanent residence

requirements.blocker_text: Requires holding a South African permanent residence permit for at least 5 years of ordinary residence before applying, per the South African Citizenship Act 88 of 1995.
requirements.fix_path: Continue holding permanent residence for the required 5-year period (see za_permanent_residence).

requirement_groups.name: Spouse of a South African citizen, 5 years on PR

requirements.blocker_text: Foreign nationals married to a South African citizen may also apply for naturalisation after 5 years holding a permanent residence permit -- per the source consulted, this is the same 5-year figure as the general track rather than a reduced one, unlike several other countries' faster spousal-naturalisation tracks documented elsewhere in this dataset.
requirements.fix_path: Continue holding permanent residence for 5 years while married to the South African citizen sponsor.

requirements.blocker_text: Minors under 21 years old who hold permanent residence may apply for citizenship through a separate, simpler process than the adult general track.

evidence_required.document: Form DHA-9 (identity document application) with 2 ID photographs, once citizenship is granted

sources.title: Western Cape Government (westerncape.gov.za, a South African provincial government portal) -- Immigration and Citizenship, confirming the 5-year-on-PR naturalisation requirement for both the general and married-to-citizen tracks, and the separate minor-under-21 process

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: this route rests on a single tier-1 provincial-government source rather than a directly-fetched dha.gov.za page or the primary Citizenship Act 88 of 1995 text itself -- kept as draft despite the tier-1 source given how much of the file's remaining structure (the married-to-citizen track's exact terms, whether any other simplified tracks exist) rests on that single source's brief treatment rather than a fuller statutory citation, consistent with this dataset's preference for corroboration before treating a route as fully verified. STRUCTURAL FINDING worth flagging clearly: unlike most other countries documented in this dataset (Poland's 2-3 year marriage track, Korea's 2-year F-6 track, Italy's 2-year domestic marriage track), South Africa's spouse-of-citizen naturalisation track does NOT appear to offer any acceleration over the general track -- both require the same 5 years of permanent residence per the single source consulted here, a genuinely different design choice worth surfacing rather than assuming marriage-based acceleration is universal across this dataset's countries. dual_citizenship_allowed is modeled true based on general knowledge that South Africa permits dual citizenship (subject to a formal retention permit requirement for South African-born citizens who naturalise elsewhere, a separate administrative process not itself modeled here), but this was not independently verified against a primary source in this specific research pass for the inbound-naturalisation direction and should be treated as the best available answer rather than fully confirmed. citizenship_after_months = 0 correctly reflects that naturalisation IS citizenship from the point of grant, per this dataset's standard convention -- the real barrier across all three groups is the preceding 5-year PR requirement (or the separate minor process), not a further wait after the naturalisation decision itself.
